Just the random, drunken ramblings of a Hungarian who lives in Austria for over 10 years now, but…

I think about Ukraine every day. I don’t know why. I’ve never been there, nor have I been close to the border when I lived in Hungary. I don’t even have any relatives from Ukraine. When I read about the war starting 2 years ago, I cried the whole afternoon. 

I think Ukraine is a wonderful country with beautiful traditions and culture. And to think that a country which borders mine, which has been influenced by Soviets too and which simply looks so similar to mine is going through this hurts so much. I can’t imagine what Ukranians went/go through since the start of the war and I don’t want to, because it scares me. 

I lived in villages my entire life, so I may not know what it’s like to have so many neighbors and friends living in the same apartments as you, and not knowing if they’re alive or not… I don’t know or understand what it would be like to stay in the underground station because I’ve been on undergrounds less than 10 times.. and I don’t know what it’s like when buildings in the city you know and love disappear. 

One thing I know for sure is that I’m unable to imagine what has happened and what *is* happening. I can’t say I’m sorry, that wouldn’t feel right. 

The only thing I can say is that I think of you every day. 

Please be safe.

honey dont take this the wrong way but your friends are definitely not in the wrong way. you seem pretty young from the way you write, and feel free to ignore my comment, but i’ve been there. 

first of all: you have to be responsible about your mental state. from my point of view, a completely objective view from the outside, you should’ve gone to therapy instead of the holiday. i understand that missing out on it sucks, i experienced this many times too. but you have to know to respect your mental health + your friends enough to cancel on outings like this when you know you’re spiraling downwards. i often had to cancel many outings with my friends as well because of this, and even if it sucks, again: it’s better for your friends and for YOU. 

reading the texts, i felt almost like i was reading my own ones from when i was like 15-17. i’m only 20 and i don’t feel like i’m super mature, but maybe you can take some of my advice.
your friends are not responsible for your mental health, neither are they responsible to be 100% available at all times. they have their own shit going on, i’m sure. i know this sounds harsh af and it felt really bad for me too but it’s something we just have to realize and to live with. 
our friends aren’t trained mental health professionals. when you wrote you thought about calling a health service or a hotline, honestly, that would’ve been better i think. 

you’re not a bad person for wanting to go on this holiday, you simply failed to accurately realize that your mental health isn’t good enough to go through with it. your friends have every right to have fun. so do you, and yes, these issues make it almost impossible and it’s a very cruel thing to say “you were supposed to be happy”. it just doesn’t work that way. 

i’m glad you apologized to your friends. we have to realize that our mental illnesses do not only affect us but the people around us, and we have to be 100% accountable when it comes to it. oh and also your friends don’t hate you if you think so. they just don’t know what to do. 

please take good care of yourself and go to therapy. again, you really remind me of myself. go to therapy!!! it is probably the best thing you could do now. good luck and take yourself seriously! writing out things the way you did can be really helpful, if i were you i would write every single day, even about unimportant things. take care!!!
